AnalyticNumberTheory.title: Arithmetic Dirichlet series and Tauberian methods, Part II: analytic number theory and zeta functions
AnalyticNumberTheory.reason: Start at the anchor's summation and conditional PNT-transfer endpoint, importing the already-built rational arithmetic and zeta/Dirichlet APIs. Retain new quantitative zero analysis, number-field/Artin comparisons, multiplicative-function estimates, and the separately sourced special-zeta and spectral branches; do not repeat the foundations.

ArithmeticStatistics.reason: Arithmetic-family parametrizations, uniform orbit counts, field/class-group asymptotics and Selmer averages are not the per-curve elliptic theory. Consume the elliptic anchor for its precise height and descent interfaces.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns.reason: Large-sieve inequalities, Bombieri-Vinogradov, bounded gaps and parity-sensitive almost-prime theorems are distinct endpoints, not restatements of analytic nonvanishing or arithmetic statistics.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.0.reason: The reviewed audit accounts for every advertised target in Mathlib or the ArithmeticDirichletSeries anchor. Remove this duplicate build stage, not its mathematics. Replace its surviving PM.0 and SV.0 consumer edges by direct library imports; AN.1 is independently retired. Preserve the Mellin hypotheses and finite-height Perron endpoint convention in the consumer obligations.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1.reason: Zeta/Dirichlet continuation, completed functional equations, principal/imprimitive Euler corrections and nonvanishing already have upstream owners. The composite-modulus character input is Mathlib, not finite-field FF.1 alone. Rewire AN.2, AN.7 and PS.1 directly; retain both accepted decomposition nodes as provenance/import records rather than new proofs.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2.keeps: Quantitative zero-free regions and their full height/conductor ranges; exceptional-zero and effectivity distinctions; construction of the analytic boundary inputs and the rational/fixed-coprime-progression PNT instances. Keep any source-required quantitative contour estimates, with their errors, separate from the qualitative Tauberian route.
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2.reason: Consume existing nonvanishing and the anchor's generic Wiener-Ikehara and psi/theta/pi transfer. Neither an upstream zero-free line nor a fixed-modulus asymptotic supplies a uniform modulus estimate.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3.keeps: Zero counting with multiplicity, explicit formulas with test-function and endpoint conditions, zero-density and basic mean-value estimates, and source-scoped short-interval/uniform progression applications (including the small-modulus input needed by SV.3). Attach RH/GRH statements from AN.6 here, using the existing RH proposition where applicable, without assuming them.
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3.reason: Perron inversion belongs to ADS Layer 6; large-sieve/bilinear inequalities belong to SV.2; Bombieri-Vinogradov belongs to SV.3. Remove the old AN.3 -> SV.2 edge before adding SV.2 -> AN.3: the latter supplies the large-sieve route to zero density. A proof of a quantitative theorem must retain its actual constants and range.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4.keeps: Arithmetic-to-analytic comparison maps for Dedekind/Hecke functions, boundary nonvanishing and prime-ideal applications, plus the Artin Euler-factor/induction interface including inertia invariants, pole orders and the distinction between meromorphic continuation and holomorphy. Retain conditional general-continuation statements from AN.6 as visible hypotheses, not theorems.
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4.reason: Import the Hecke character carrier from GlobalNumberFields Layer 9, local/global Tate analytic theory from AL.0-1, the real class-number residue from Mathlib, and density/transfer from ADS. Preserve the accepted Tate proof records, including the Z1-Z3 admissible-class extension rather than only Schwartz-Bruhat functions, at their new analytic owner, with the ideal-series comparison at AN.4. AN.4 instantiates the conditional anchor theorem; no reverse edge into the anchor is proposed. The current Artin rational-induction source only supplies a near-line route; a whole-plane route needs its additional induction proof, not an unproved root extraction.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5.reason: Keep Halasz/pretentious global mean values, smooth-number and divisor problems, L-function moments and their source-scoped random-matrix predictions, and the Beurling-prime extension with explicit axioms. Arithmetic-family distributions at ST.5 and almost-everywhere/correlation laws at PM.1/PM.5 are different targets; shared model vocabulary does not justify deleting them.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6.reason: This is an export/register stage, not a separate mathematical construction. Attach zero-free contracts to AN.2, density/explicit-formula and RH/GRH statements to AN.3, general conditional analytic statements to AN.4, distribution hypotheses to SV.3 and prime-tuple statements to SV.4. Keep provenance and compatibility obligations in the report. The atlas records no consumers of this node.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.7.keeps: The general Lerch/parameter-singularity and branch analysis not supplied by the real-circle Hurwitz/exponential-zeta APIs, together with exact comparison maps and any genuinely missing special-value results. Preserve every original Hurwitz and cyclotomic-Dirichlet target as an import or explicit comparison.
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.7.reason: Reuse Mathlib Hurwitz and exponential zeta, their continuation/functional equations and special values. For standard Phi(z,s,a), exponential zeta is z*Phi(z,s,1), not Phi(z,s,1); justify the initial convergence domain and subsequent continuation. A UnitAddCircle parameter is not a general complex parameter.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8.keeps: Selected several-variable Dirichlet series and prehomogeneous zeta integrals, analytic local integrals/density formulas, convergence, continuation and matrix functional equations, with comparison from the selected integral orbit data to the analytic coefficients. Preserve LD.3, AL.0 and AA.2 inputs and the distinct multiple-zeta-values boundary.
AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8.reason: ST.1 owns the shared arithmetic orbit parametrizations, invariants and stabilizer dictionaries; ST.0 owns arithmetic-family/local-condition normalization data. AN.8 owns the analytic zeta construction, not a second orbit bijection. Different local-density objects in sieves, circle-method singular series and zeta integrals are related only by proved comparisons, not identified by name.

AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9.reason: Retain both the selected Selberg/spectral-zeta and regularized-determinant branch, and the Bost-Connes algebra, time evolution, KMS and arithmetic-action branch. Trace/spectral prerequisites are imports, not proofs of the new zeta identities. No RH consequence or unproved spectral interpretation is imported.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0.keeps: Arithmetic families with their equivalence relations, discriminant/general-height orderings, local conditions, automorphism weights, bounded-height finiteness, and the comparison of each selected family convention to the canonical carrier.
ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0.reason: For elliptic curves over Q, import EC Layer 8's minimal-pair short-equation height and finiteness of isomorphism classes. Do not replace this by point heights, a DVR-minimal long model, or the false finiteness of all rational equations.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.1.reason: Keep source-scoped integral orbit parametrizations for number rings and genus-one models, inverse/stabilizer/degenerate-orbit and local-solubility proofs. The binary-quartic/genus-one realization is not the etale-algebra square-class carrier in EC Layer 6. Own the comparison to the explicit/cohomological Selmer models, importing EC Layers 6-7 rather than rebuilding descent. Export the shared orbit data to AN.8.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2.keeps: Uniform arithmetic-family lattice/orbit counts, fundamental-domain applicability, cusp and reducible contributions, and uniform tail estimates for passage from finitely many to infinitely many local conditions.
ArithmeticStatistics:ST.2.reason: Consume source-scoped generic lattice-point estimates rather than rebuilding their general carrier and theorem. The required uniform arithmetic-family errors and cusp/tail analysis are not supplied by generic bounded-region counting.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3.keeps: Selected field-counting and class-group asymptotics and moments, with degree, signature, Galois-group, local-condition and automorphism-weight restrictions retained.
ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3.reason: The per-field analytic class-number formula and analytic comparisons are imported inputs, not a second construction. Neither a residue formula nor ideal counting proves a field-family or class-group distribution theorem.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4.keeps: Source-scoped Bhargava-Shankar Selmer averages and statistical rank deductions, including family ordering, uniform local-solubility counts and the comparison from the selected orbit parametrization to canonical Selmer groups.
ArithmeticStatistics:ST.4.reason: Per-curve Mordell-Weil, explicit descent, general Selmer/Sha objects and the exact sequence belong to the elliptic anchor. Its rank inequality requires finite generation and a finite subgroup containing the descent image; it does not prove Selmer finiteness or Sha finiteness by itself. The averaging theorem is new mathematics here.

ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5.reason: Keep higher arithmetic-family moments, local distributions, source-scoped function-field comparisons and conjectural models. An L-value moment ensemble at AN.5 is not the same measure or sample space, so no statistical theorem is dropped on the basis of random-matrix vocabulary.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.0.keeps: Sieve dimension, actual remainder-sum level-of-distribution predicates and estimates, the missing sieve inclusion-exclusion specialization, and missing lower-bound constructions.
SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.0.reason: Use the existing finite weighted BoundingSieve data, rem, siftedSum and errSum. SelbergSieve.level is a weight-truncation parameter, not a theorem controlling the sum of absolute remainders. Retain every original bound target that the library does not yet supply.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.1.keeps: Brun weights, completion/optimization of the Selberg argument beyond existing diagonalization, the fundamental lemma with its actual range, upper-bound applications and the parity limitation.
SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.1.reason: Reuse Mathlib's lambdaSquared and upperMoebius_lambdaSquared (including weights(1)=1) and the existing main-term/error inequality. Do not schedule a second proof of the supplied upper-bound construction.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2.keeps: Additive and multiplicative large-sieve inequalities, their finite-dimensional duality argument, and source-scoped Vaughan/Type I-II bilinear decompositions with principal and diagonal terms and actual loss factors.
SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.2.reason: Consume primitive-character/conductor/orthogonality APIs, not a new character carrier. Delete the old requires AN.3: this foundational inequality stage does not depend on zero-density estimates. Its exports may instead be consumed by AN.3; BV remains downstream in SV.3.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.3.reason: Own Bombieri-Vinogradov with forall A exists B, the stated logarithmic loss, range Q <= x^(1/2)/(log x)^B and its precise sum/max convention. Consume AN.3's source-scoped small-modulus/zero-density inputs and SV.2. Own the explicit stronger-distribution hypotheses formerly registered in AN.6; none is silently unconditional.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.4.reason: Own admissible tuples, Maynard multidimensional weights, quadratic-form asymptotics and positivity, and the actual finite-gap theorem. Own the prime-tuple conjecture statement formerly registered in AN.6, separately from the proven result. A bounded-gap conclusion is not the twin-prime conjecture; AC.4 retains its own majorant pseudorandomness proof.

SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.5.reason: Keep beta/weighted sieves, the source-selected Chen branch and the affine-sieve branch, with their distinct parity-breaking, bilinear, spectral-gap and orbit hypotheses. Reuse the existing almost-prime count with multiplicity; no prime-pattern target is deleted because its proof is not yet built.
